entries.title: dead code: a caller in another file is found without an import edge
entries.summary: `get_dead_code_v2` no longer reports a function as having no caller when its only caller is in another file the import graph does not join to it. For a language that records no call reference the tool read the function's own file and its importers; a Clojure `:require`, an Elixir `alias`, an Erlang remote call, a Bash `source` and two C files sharing a header give the graph no such edge. A function still without a caller is now asked of every other text-read code file. The trade is toward not reporting: a function nothing calls is no longer reported when another code file names it in a comment, an Elixir `@spec`, an Erlang `-export` or a doc comment above a C prototype. The CHANGELOG lists every measured case in both directions.

entries.title: dead code: a file is read as text wherever its language records no call
entries.summary: `get_dead_code_v2` no longer reports a called function as having no caller because its language records no call reference while another language in the repository does. It chose between call references and file text with one repository-wide question; the choice is now made per file, by what the index holds for that file's language. Measured on Clojure, Elixir, Erlang, PHP, C, Bash and Dart beside Python. When text was read for a caller the response says so in a new key, `callers_read_as_text`. Also in this release: the module-level sweep no longer searches a file's whole module-level text once per function whose name is not a plain identifier (a Clojure file of 8,000 functions went from 15.43 s to 0.18 s). Still reported: a caller in another file where the import graph holds no edge, and a name ending in `?` or `!`.

entries.title: the dead-code text fallback reads a file once
entries.summary: `get_dead_code_v2` on an index that holds no call reference no longer costs time quadratic in the functions of one file. It decided whether each function had a caller by splitting the function's whole file, joining the lines outside it and searching the result, once per function. On one generated Python file the tool took 3.38 s at 2,872 functions, 13.68 s at 5,655 and 53.42 s at 11,109; the same three now take 0.05 s, 0.12 s and 0.22 s. Each file is read, split and tokenised once, and the answers are unchanged. The fallback's peak memory is higher (34.1 MB against 10.0 MB on this repository's source). A repository whose index holds any call reference never took this path.

entries.title: the index CLI chooses the index identity, and an existing directory is a local target
entries.summary: `jcodemunch-mcp index <path> --identity-mode local|git` chooses how a local path is keyed in the index store; the CLI always ran in `config` mode before. An explicit mode on a GitHub target is refused before any network call. A directory that exists is now a local target however it is spelled (`proj/`, `proj/sub`, `~/proj`), where the CLI sent those spellings to the GitHub indexer. That moves one command with no option: `index owner/repo` or `index github.com/owner/repo`, run where a directory of that relative name exists, now indexes the directory. `https://github.com/owner/repo` forces the remote. Requested by @sKlat-beep (#1017).
